newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rice exporters urged to mull shipping alternatives.
newsitem.headline: Rice exporters urged to mull shipping alternatives.

text.p: Rice exporters will have to consider alternatives to shipping their goods and find ways to relieve congestion in ports, a shipping industry analyst said on Friday.

Lawrence Pupkin, general manager of Fearnleys Ltd in Thailand, said in a report to the Asia rice conference in Singapore that due to a "thinning of the fleet that the rice and similar trades depend (on), alternative forms of sea transport are likely necessary."
"The vessels of significance to the rice trade have mostly been those in the 10,000 to 18,000 deadweight sector. Approximately 83 percent of this fleet is now over 15 years of age," the report said.
Called tweendeckers, they are not being replaced as the bulk carrier industry increasingly shifts to larger bulk vessels.
"In order to ship in larger sizes, there would be a need (for a) fundamental changes to increasingly ship in bulk rather than bags," Pupkin said.

One alternative for exporters is parceling, the practice of putting together various cargoes together on large vessels. Another is containerisation, which has the advantage of allowing the cargo to be moved in further inland.
"But containers tend to be an expensive form of sea transport and is more suited to very high value cargoes," the report said.
Another problem which must be addressed urgently in the Asia-Pacific region is port congestion.
"Extensive and ever increasing exportation and importation of agricultural products, especially within Asia and the Pacific, has caused mind boggling congestion" at many ports, the report said.

"Cargoes which should take only some few days to load have more than occasionally had vessels wait off the port for up to two or three months. Either way, someone at either end pays for these delays caused to the ship," the report concluded.
The Asia-Pacific region contains three of the world's leading rice exporters.

Thailand is the world's biggest rice exporter. Its rivals include India and Vietnam. All three countries have said they must modernise port facilities to tackle the increasing amount of cargoes being handled in their ports.
